issues.title: 22 Node, Bun and Deno stacks benchmarked
issues.html:
#​647 — November 12, 2026


Read on the Web







An Experimental 'Green Threads' Implementation for Node — James has opened a PR that adds a new, lightweight kind of worker that shares a small pool of OS threads, with each worker getting its own V8 isolate (but no Node APIs). His numbers show a thousand of them using about 1GB of memory vs 6.7GB for regular worker threads. Early days, but a promising idea that deserves feedback.

James M Snell



Debug Errors and Agents Faster: Sentry Changelog Live — A walkthrough of what’s new for debugging errors and performance issues, including fixing production bugs with Seer and tracing the agents you build. Live Q&A. Nov 18, 10am PT. Save your spot.

Sentry sponsor



🔒 This Week's Node.js Security Releases — Node v26.13.1, v24.22.3 and v22.23.5 patch a lot of HTTP/2 and TLS flaws, plus others in zlib and the permission model (seven are rated 'high' in severity). The worst bug can allow a remote client to read memory belonging to other connections. v26 and v24 also get last week's Undici fixes.

The Node.js Project



🤖 Five of the bugs were reported by Chris Rohlf "in collaboration with Claude and Anthropic Research", with another credited to Trail of Bits (OpenAI).



What's New in Node.js 27 — The co-author of Node.js Design Patterns has put together an example-led tour of the latest (alpha) Node release, going from the new iterator helpers and promise-based node:net/promises API to the now-unflagged virtual file system, plus the v27 breaking changes to get prepared for.

Luciano Mammino



IN BRIEF:

  • The browser-style Web Worker API is now enabled by default on Node's main branch, so expect it in a future Node 27 alpha release.

  • Sadly, JavaScript function hosting platform Val Town is winding down. Tom MacWright, who advocated for its move to Deno (from vm2), wrote this week about that choice saying Deno's sandbox never let them down.

  • Netlify has introduced Netlify Server, a long-running Node-powered backend process for WebSockets and in-memory state, now in early access.

  • An open PR proposes a built-in node:yaml module for parsing YAML.

  • 📊 The State of JavaScript 2026 survey is now open to take.



How X is Rebuilding Its Web App on Fastify and Node 26 — X is replacing three servers with one built on Fastify and Platformatic Watt, running worker threads on Node 26. Yagiz covers the streaming architecture, the event loop stalls they had to fix, and how it's making X faster on the Web.

Yagiz Nizipli (X Engineering)



Keep Your CI Workflow While Upgrading the Runner at Half the Cost — Switch to a WarpBuild runner in your Node job and see faster builds. Try it with $50 in free credits using START50.

WarpBuild sponsor



A Malicious npm Release, Published via Trusted Publishing — A tour of the process and code behind the recent hijacking of Ethersphere's bee-js release process and how a backdoored version was published with valid provenance.

Socket Research Team



Your JS Error Is Lying to You — If you've ever seen "err":{} logged for an error that definitely had a message, Gábor's look into what an Error loses between creation and the log line could be helpful.

Gábor Koós



🛠 Code & Tools





forges: One Client for GitHub, GitLab and Other Git Forges — From Nuxt's lead maintainer, this is a single typed client for working with issues, PRs, notifications, checks and webhooks across GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket, Codeberg, Gitea, Azure DevOps and more.

Daniel Roe



AWS Emulator: An Official Local Emulator for AWS APIs — It's built in Rust, but there's now an officially supported way to point your AWS SDK or CLI at a local endpoint covering hundreds of its service interfaces. In the release post, Amazon suggests it's largely aimed at agents, while also revealing the emulator itself was built with agents (and how).

Amazon Web Services



chrome-capture: Record a Chrome Tab at 60 FPS to MP4 — A neat, compact tool you can run with npx to record a Chrome 153+ tab at high quality to an MP4 file with no ffmpeg needed.

Paul Irish



  • Playwright 1.65 – Microsoft's browser automation library. Its test runner can now run under Bun too (with a few caveats), and there are a few potentially breaking changes for existing users who upgrade…

  • vlt 1.7 – The package manager adds vlt deploy for copying a workspace and production dependencies into a standalone folder, and now pins git dependencies to a commit.

  • Postgres.js 4.1 – Follows the recent big 4.0 release with sql.batch(), a query_timeout option, and restored Node 18 support.



📰 Classifieds



⏱️ JSON in Postgres: still fast at 1M rows? ExoBench benchmarks your query at scale, from Claude or Cursor. Now in preview.

🔓 Your auth validates once at login. After that, a stolen cookie works from anywhere. Fingerprint catches it. Try it free.



📊  22 JavaScript Stack Combos Benchmarked





▶ I Tested Every JavaScript Runtime — A fun benchmark of the same Postgres-backed API app running on Node, Bun and Deno using each of their popular frameworks. In his tests, runtime choice made a bigger difference than framework choice. The code and full results are on GitHub too.

Arjay McCandless

issues.title: Node 27's first alpha brings breaking changes
issues.html:
#​646 — November 5, 2026


Read on the Web







Node.js 27 Alpha: The First Release Under Node's New Schedule — Under Node's new release model, each major release spends six months in alpha before stable release — so v27's final is due next April. Alphas are built from main with breaking changes, and are meant for library authors / testing rather than prod.



  • V8 15.6 brings Math.sumPrecise(), Iterator.zip() and other iterator helpers by default, and import defer and immutable ArrayBuffers are available behind flags.

  • There's a new default heap limit of half of physical memory (clamped between 256MB and 4GB), and memory held by Buffers counts toward it. If you relied on the old defaults, you can set --max-old-space-size.

  • v8.serialize(), structuredClone() and postMessage() use a new format unreadable by older Nodes, so take care with mixed-version use.

  • fs.glob is now implemented natively, there's an experimental net/promises API, and --allow-env joins the permission model.

  • npm 12(.1) is now bundled so there are breaking changes to be aware of.

Rafael Gonzaga (Node.js Release Team)



Stop Babysitting Chats. Run Your Own Software Factory — A chat per agent, each one waiting on you. CodeAF does the middle: it splits the work, runs the parts in parallel, tests what came back, merges what passed and asks only when it must. #1 of ten coding harnesses on DeepSWE, at the lowest cost per fix.

CodeAF by AgentField AI sponsor



Notable V8 Changes from Node.js 26 to 27 — Further to the Node 27 updates above, here's a fantastic roundup of what new things V8 15.6 brings to the table for Node users. It's a big update as Node 26 uses V8 14.6.

Joyee Cheung



'Nothing Installs at Our Company Until It's a Week Old' — Bruno put a proxy between his company and npm that refuses releases under seven days old. Twelve days on, he shares the numbers, the lockfiles it broke, and some practical advice if you want to do it yourself.

Bruno Jurković



IN BRIEF:

  • Express's October security roundup covers DoS fixes in body-parser and multer, plus its official line on the Brotli flaw: upgrade Node (but there's a workaround if you can't).

  • Vercel builds now block known-malicious npm package versions before and during install, with no configuration needed.

  • 🔒 It's a busy week for server framework security updates: Fastify 5.12.8 heads a wave of Fastify advisories including a critical proxy prefix escape, Hono 4.13.16 fixes several issues, and Nuxt 4.6.4 and Nitro 2.13.6 close eleven more.



Signing and Attestations Across Package Registries — A registry-by-registry survey of what npm, PyPI, RubyGems, crates.io, Go and others sign, which produce provenance attestations, and which offer trusted publishing, concluding with a handy comparison table.

Andrew Nesbitt



💡 Related: mise now verifies npm provenance by default and pins tools it installs to the repos that built them.



Parcel 3 Alpha: The Bundler Now Rewritten in Rust — Parcel's core is now a standalone Rust binary, with builds up to 100x faster on a large monorepo as a result. Plugins can be written in Rust, Go, Swift or C, or in JS/TS on a custom runtime, and there's HMR for Node targets.

Devon Govett



📄 Fuzzers vs. AI: Six Months of Hunting V8 Bugs – Fuzzilli and the BigSleep LLM agent compared on real production counts. Google Project Zero

📄 No, npm, estee Is Not a Typo of testem – On npm's typosquat heuristic and the math of four-letter names. Shane Friedman



🛠 Code & Tools





Wiki.js 3: A Modern Wiki App Built on Node — A mature project packed with features and an ecosystem of modules to integrate with other systems. Note that it's AGPL licensed. GitHub repo.

Requarks



Should You Use a Log or a Metric? — Learn when to reach for a log and when for a metric, with one signup handler as the example. Read the post.

Sentry sponsor



Postgres.js 4.0: A Ground-Up Rewrite of the Popular Postgres Client — The public API is largely unchanged, but the rewrite gains a scheduler that stops fast queries waiting behind slow ones, AbortSignal support, and more. It's ESM-only and param typing has changed, so the upgrade guide is a must-read for users.

Rasmus Porsager



NestJS 12.3: A Native node:http Platform Adapter — The server framework has long sat on top of Express or Fastify. A third adapter now runs on node:http, with Express-style request helpers but no Express dependency.

NestJS



jsdom 31.0: A New CSS Engine and a Switch to @napi-rs/canvas — The pure-JS DOM behind countless test suites gains an integrated CSS implementation (supporting cascade layers, nesting, and @scope), swaps canvas for @napi-rs/canvas, and pauses parsing at blocking scripts.

Domenic Denicola et al.



Vitest 5.1: Run Only the Tests Your Last Change Affected — An experimental --since-last-run flag records which files each test loaded and reruns only what your edits touched, with no Git involved.

Vitest Team



Nitro v3 Reaches Release Candidate — The server toolkit under Nuxt and friends gets a frozen API, an install a fraction of v2's size, Vitest-based route testing, and an experimental nitro serve that runs your source in production with no build step.

Pooya Parsa (UnJS)



📰 Classifieds



🤖 Your free AI tier is being farmed by a person with fifty accounts. Fingerprint recognizes the device behind every signup. Try it free.

🕐 Calgary or Winnipeg an hour off since Nov 1? Node 22 and 24 bundle tz data an OS update won't fix. Tested fixes from an AI-run company.





  • ora 10 – The elegant terminal spinner (above) now requires Node 22 and erases only its own frame, leaving your program's output intact.

  • Vite+ 1.5 – VoidZero's all-in-one toolchain adds a node --import vite-plus/register hook so the built-in test runner, AVA or NODE_OPTIONS can run TypeScript through its loader.

  • Got 16.2 – Sindre Sorhus's "human-friendly" HTTP request library. .json() now accepts a Standard Schema validator (Zod, Valibot, ArkType) so responses are validated and typed in one call.

  • fast-json-stringify 7.3 – Fastify's serializer gains an option to lean on V8's new JSON.stringify fast path (in Node 25+) for double the throughput.

  • express-fileupload 1.6 – Fixes a ReDoS in its Content-Type check where a run of semicolons could stall the event loop.

  • marked-terminal 8.0 – Render Markdown in the terminal. A TypeScript rewrite with a new mt CLI and support for images via the Kitty and iTerm2 graphics protocols.

  • Koa 3.3 – A hardening-flavored minor for the Express successor.

issues.title: Node security releases to fix a Brotli flaw
issues.html:
#​645 — October 29, 2026


Read on the Web







Node.js 26 'Lithium' Is Now the Active LTS Line — Node.js 26.13.0 promotes Node 26 to long-term support, with updates through April 2029, making it the new line to target for production. Node 24 has moved into maintenance and 22 remains in maintenance until April 2027 – the Node releases page has a neat graph to visualize this.

Node.js Release Team



💡 Meanwhile, Node 27's first alpha, the first release under Node's new annual release schedule, is being prepared and should land later today.



Build an Agent that Never Sleeps — Most agents stop when you close the chat. Learn to build one that keeps working: it triages incidents, asks your permission before risky fixes, and picks up where it left off after a crash.

Master.dev sponsor



Upgrade Now: Node's October Security Releases Fix a Brotli Flaw — Last week's releases (26.12.1, 24.22.1 and 22.23.4) fix ten CVEs, including a flaw in the bundled Brotli decoder, since dubbed Node2Shell, that can allow remote code execution if apps decompress malicious Brotli data, such as through node:zlib.

Node.js Project



IN BRIEF:

  • 🔒 Express explains a body-parser bug where trailing bytes after a gzipped body can let a request crash a process. It's fixed in 2.4.0 and 1.20.9.

  • After a TSC vote, Node has merged a new experimental flag to strip types from TypeScript in node_modules, but only inside packages marked private, such as monorepo workspaces.

  • Electron 45 is out, moving to Chromium 156, V8 15.6 and Node 24.22. Sandboxed preload scripts lose the Buffer and setImmediate globals, and Electron 42 has now reached its end-of-life.

  • GitHub Actions workflow lockfiles are now generally available letting you pin actions and their dependencies in participating workflows.



The Web Can't Afford a JavaScript Runtime Monoculture — With Deno's runtime set to wind down after its team's move to Cloudflare, the field of major server-side runtimes could narrow to Node, Bun and workerd. An analyst draws on IE6, Chromium's dominance and the io.js fork to argue why that might worry us.

Kate Holterhoff (RedMonk)



💡 Meanwhile, Deno's team says it's working on getting Deno into a foundation, and an initial fork, Ende, has appeared.



Reylo: Import .sql Files into TypeScript with Full Type Inference — From the creator of Zod: write queries in plain .sql files and import them into TypeScript, with row and param types inferred from the SQL. No codegen step, but it relies on TypeScript 7.1's new content mappers (now in beta).

Colin McDonnell



Up to 10x Faster Postgres for I/O-Heavy Workloads — Managed Postgres on local NVMe, natively integrated with ClickHouse for real-time analytics.

ClickHouse Managed Postgres sponsor



📄 Why Parallel Publishes Can Briefly Break npm Installs – Monorepo releases can land before their own dependencies. Evert Pot (vlt)

📄 node:vfs: What Shipped, How It Works, and Its Limits Matteo Collina (Platformatic)



🛠 Code & Tools





Dependency Cruiser 18.7: Validate and Visualize Your Dependencies — Set rules about what may depend on what (no circular imports, say, or no reaching into another package's internals), check them in CI, and render the results as graphs. There's a page of graphs for real projects like Yarn and React.

Sander Verweij



OpenTelemetry JS 3.0 Released — OpenTelemetry's JavaScript SDK now ships dual ESM/CommonJS builds with strict exports maps (so deep imports break), and merges the Node, web and base trace SDKs into a single package.

OpenTelemetry



💡 Meanwhile, a new repo under the Node.js org, microtel, prototypes a minimal OpenTelemetry implementation meant to eventually land in Node itself.



bundle: Ship a Node App as One Signed File — Freezes a Node app and its dependency tree into a signed ZIP that Node 26's experimental virtual file system runs directly, with no npm install needed. Its author wrote several of the core VFS pieces it builds on.

Philipp Dunkel



gpuix-svelte: Native Desktop Apps from Svelte, No Webview — Draws Svelte components natively using GPUI, the GPU-powered UI framework behind Zed, while your code runs in Node or Bun. Experimental, as it relies on Svelte's unreleased custom renderers feature. GitHub repo.

Stanislav Khromov



sqlite-js-stream: Litestream, Rewritten for Node by an AI Agent — Litestream continuously streams SQLite's write-ahead log to S3 so a single-file database can be recovered. Platformatic has ported the Go tool to TypeScript running directly on node:sqlite.

Matteo Collina (Platformatic)



📰 Classifieds



🛒 AI agents are completing purchases for real customers. Fingerprint identifies them so you don’t block a sale. Learn how.

📄 Invoices in, JSON out. Pull line items, totals, dates and vendor details from invoice PDFs with Foxit's extraction API.





  • Chokidar 6.0 – A rewrite of the popular file watching library (above). v6 confirms changes against the filesystem before emitting events.

  • Verdaccio 7.0 – Lightweight, self-hostable private npm registry and proxy. v7 adds staged publishing and 2FA and requires Node 24+.

  • AVA 8.2 – Long-standing Node test runner. v8.1 can be up to 50% faster on many common workloads while 8.2 rolls out some fixes.

  • path-to-regexp 9.0 – Library that turns paths like /user/:name into regular expressions, as used by Express. Now ESM-only, with a subtle change to how ambiguous segments match.

  • Directus 12.6 – Connect any SQL database and get instant REST and GraphQL APIs, a visual management Studio, and a native MCP server for AI agents.

  • Croner 11.0 – Library to trigger functions or evaluate cron expressions.
